QF.id: XVI Code of Conduct and Investor Protection_19

answer.text: A broker trading ahead of a client's large order to benefit from the expected price impact
Being the first to place an order each morning
Trading in the most actively traded commodity
Placing orders at the best available price

explanation.text: The Logic: Front-running, in the context of broker conduct, refers to a broker trading on their own proprietary account (or for a related account) ahead of a pending large client order in the same or a related instrument, in order to profit from the price impact that the client's order is expected to cause. It is a recognised form of market abuse and a breach of the broker's duty to act in the client's interest. The Trap: Front-running is not about being the first to place an order each morning, trading in the most actively traded commodity, or placing orders at the best available price — none of those describe trading ahead of a specific client's pending order. It is a precise conflict-of-interest concept based on misuse of advance knowledge of client orders. Note: The term "front-running" and its specific definition (broker trading ahead of a client order) were not located in the cited Series XVI pages (p.130, p.191-p.193, p.196-p.199, p.203-p.204), which set out the general code of conduct around manipulation, deception, conflict of interest, and misuse of client information without defining front-running by name. The framing above relies on general securities-market regulatory knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
